name: Guadeloupe

findings.summary: Orange's Kanawa submarine cable linking French Guiana, Martinique and Guadeloupe entered service, with Infinera supplying the optical transmission platform on the Martinique-Guadeloupe segment.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment rule: Infinera (US-headquartered at the source date) supplies the optical line equipment, so pole us; Orange (France) owns the cable. Any later change in Infinera ownership was not verified in this run. Only one opened source, a vendor press release, so not corroborated. Pre-2020 and still_current not confirmed.

findings.summary: Canal+ Telecom inaugurated a Tier III-rated data centre at Moudong in the Jarry zone of Baie-Mahault, offering secure hosting services to local authorities and businesses. Capacity and investment were not stated.
findings.analyst_inference: French-controller treatment: SPEC defines domestic as a controller from this same territory, so metropolitan French or EU controllers are coded third for Guadeloupe even though it is a French department. Canal+ Telecom is taken to be controlled by Groupe Canal+ (France), hence third; its corporate parentage was not confirmed in an opened source. Small general-purpose facility, not an AI campus.

findings.financier: European Union, Connecting Europe Facility (CEF Digital), about 70%
findings.summary: Groupe Canal+ presented CaribbeanConnect, a 300 Gb/s submarine cable linking Puerto Rico, Guadeloupe and Martinique to replace an end-of-life cable; about 6 million euros, roughly 70% EU CEF Digital co-financed, commissioning expected 2025.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null because the cable and terminal equipment vendors are not named; under the equipment rule the vendor, not the owner, sets the pole. Tier 4 because EU co-financing is stated as committed; operation not confirmed. EUR value not converted (no source-date rate obtained), so values null.
